newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan car output expected to continue rising.
newsitem.headline: Japan car output expected to continue rising.

text.p: Japan's automobile production is likely to continue rising in the months ahead, fuelled by increasing exports, after racking up strong gains in April, industry sources said.

The Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association (JAMA) said on Monday that Japan's domestic vehicle production rose 11.4 percent in April from a year earlier to 887,150 vehicles, marking the second consecutive month of year-on-year growth.

"The gain stemmed from higher exports and higher production of new models for the domestic market ahead of their official launch," a JAMA official said. "Higher production is expected to continue for the time being."
In April, Japanese carmakers launched six new models, in hopes that a flood of new offerings would help offset the dampening effects of an increase in Japan's national sales tax on April 1, he said.
He also noted that Nissan Motor Co Ltd and Toyota Motor Corp each followed with another new model in May.
"The gain in April production resulted from higher exports and strong domestic demand," a spokesman for Honda Motor Co Ltd said.

"Out North American units are operating at full capacity. We still need to export Civic (four-door sedans) from Japan because of strong demand there and we started exporting the CR-V light sport-utility vehicle to the U.S. in January," he added.
Honda's April exports rose a steep 23.2 percent from a year earlier to 107,771 units.
Honda still has a backlog of domestic orders for recreational vehicle models such as the S-MX, the Step Wagon minivan and the recently launched Life 660CC Mini RV, he said.

Honda also plans to export 20,000 Accords from Japan to the U.S. between April and July, when its Ohio plant will temporarily halt production to retool for a remodelled version of the sedan, to be launched in the summer, the spokesman said.
Spokesmen from Toyota, Nissan and Mitsubishi Motors Corp also said the higher April output mainly stemmed from higher exports.
Toyota's exports in April rose 8.1 percent to 290,675, while Nissan's increased 17.8 percent to 135,542.
JAMA said Japan's exports in April rose about 19 percent from a year earlier, although vehicle exports had been dull in the 17 months through May 1996 due to the strong yen.
The major Japanese carmakers also expect their domestic production to continue marking year-on-year gains for the next few months.
Signs are emerging, however, that strong export growth at Japan's carmakers could rekindle a U.S.-Japan trade spat.
U.S. government figures released last Wednesday showed the U.S. trade deficit with Japan grew 8.3 percent in March to $4.6 billion.
U.S. automobile industry officials said the figures show the weak yen is continuing to hurt domestic U.S. carmakers.
